10.t: Working with data: fish membranes and temperature
q: Calculate the mean change in unsaturated fatty acids per °C.
Explain how more unsaturated fatty acids help fish in cold water.
The kinks in unsaturated tails stop the phospholipids packing tightly, so the membrane stays fluid in the cold and its proteins keep working.
Describe and explain the change in cholesterol.
Cholesterol doubles from 8% to 16% as temperature rises. It restricts the movement of phospholipids, stopping the membrane becoming too fluid in warm water.
Membrane fluidity hardly changes. Explain what this shows.
The changes in lipid composition compensate for temperature, keeping fluidity almost constant: a form of homeostasis in the membrane.
Predict the membrane composition of fish moved from 25 °C to 5 °C, after 6 weeks.
About 68% unsaturated fatty acids and 8% cholesterol, like fish kept at 5 °C.
